videos.title: Sitting so the arms can move
videos.description: Bench height, distance, and a quiet core so wrists stay free.

notes.abstract: Piano posture is balanced height and distance — not a rigid “correct” pose.
points: Sit so elbows are slightly below the key tops.
Keep a soft wrist and long fingers.
Leave space so you can shift laterally without leaning hard.
notes.conclusion: If wrists ache early, check bench height before blaming technique.

videos.title: Hands separate before hands together
videos.description: Learn each hand cleanly, then merge at half speed.

notes.abstract: Together-too-soon creates guesswork; separate practice builds maps.
points: Master the harder hand alone first.
Merge at a tempo where both hands stay accurate.
Only then raise speed in small steps.
notes.conclusion: Speed without a clean map just rehearses mistakes.

videos.title: Five-finger patterns that stick
videos.description: Simple scale and pattern drills for even tone.

notes.abstract: Evenness comes from listening, not from pressing harder.
points: Play soft and listen for matching attacks.
Keep fingers close to the keys.
Stop when unevenness appears — reset slower.
notes.conclusion: Loud and uneven is not progress — soft and even is.

videos.title: Pedal as color, not blur
videos.description: Change pedal with harmony, not with every bar line.

notes.abstract: Pedal clarifies harmony when timed to changes, and muddies when held too long.
points: Change on the new harmony, not early.
Listen for blur and clear it immediately.
notes.conclusion: If the texture turns cloudy, you are pedaling through a change.

videos.title: Performance run without panic
videos.description: Mock run-throughs: start, recover, finish — even after a stumble.

notes.abstract: Performance practice trains recovery, not perfection in the practice room only.
points: Do full run-throughs without stopping for tiny errors.
Mark two restart points you can find under pressure.
Record one take and review tomorrow.
notes.conclusion: Stopping at every mistake teaches stopping — practice continuing.

resorts.name: 4-day piano week
resorts.summary: A light weekly rotation that balances technique and pieces.
resorts.intro:
Day A: scales + reading
Day B: repertoire slow
Day C: hands separate hard spots
Day D: full run + notes

Keep sessions short enough to stay focused.

resorts.name: Bench & keyboard setup
resorts.summary: Height, distance, and digital vs acoustic basics.
resorts.intro:
Match bench height so wrists stay level. Sit far enough to move laterally.

On digital pianos, check weighted keys and a sustain pedal that feels consistent.
